text.arabic_uthmani: وَٱلْبُدْنَ جَعَلْنَٰهَا لَكُم مِّن شَعَٰٓئِرِ ٱللَّهِ لَكُمْ فِيهَا خَيْرٌۭ ۖ فَٱذْكُرُوا۟ ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا صَوَآفَّ ۖ فَإِذَا وَجَبَتْ جُنُوبُهَا فَكُلُوا۟ مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُوا۟ ٱلْقَانِعَ وَٱلْمُعْتَرَّ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ سَخَّرْنَٰهَا لَكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ

words.gloss_range: resumptive/additive conjunction opening a new sacrificial-procedure unit while preserving continuity with 22:35
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens a new procedural unit without severing it from the preceding worshipper portrait. The conjunction keeps continuity with 22:35 while shifting the scene from interior devotion to the handling of the sacrificial bodies.

topics.headline: resumptive procedure opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah both continues the pilgrimage passage and starts a fresh procedure for the large offerings.
topics.reason: QAC allows either resumption or coordination, and the CRITICAL rows converge on a continuous but new sacrificial-instruction unit.

words.gloss_range: definite fronted accusative for the large sacrificial animals, resumed by the later feminine pronoun
words.root_gloss_range: body, bodily mass, and sacrificial-animal body; local sense is the appointed large offering, with body-as-sign pressure retained

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: perfect 1st person plural with attached feminine pronoun -hā (referring to al-budna); doubly transitive (object 1 = -hā, object 2 = min shaʿāʾir)

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْبُدْنَ}} ({{tr:al-budna}}) is placed first as a fronted accusative object and then resumed by the pronoun in {{ar:جَعَلْنَٰهَا}} ({{tr:jaʿalnāhā}}), so the animals become the discourse topic before the divine appointment is stated. The body-root keeps the offering materially visible: these are not generic livestock but substantial sacrificial bodies made into signs. The rare b-d-n field also lets 10:92 stand in the background, where a body becomes a sign, while local grammar keeps the referent here to the appointed offerings.

topics.headline: fronted sacrificial bodies
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the animal bodies become the topic before the divine action is predicated of them.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as accusative and fronted/topicalized, and the following pronoun resumes it.

topics.headline: plural form and variant limits
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that accepted variants adjust the topic/case or plural weight, while the local standard form remains an accusative plural offering noun.
topics.reason: The variants are useful apparatus, but they do not replace the local accusative fronted-object analysis.

topics.headline: rare body-as-sign echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears that the rare body root can turn bodily matter into a sign, with 10:92 as a contrast rather than a governing scene.
topics.reason: The cross-reference is concrete and meaningful, but local sense remains sacrificial animals rather than Pharaoh’s preserved body.

words.gloss_range: completed divine appointment of the animals into the category of God’s ritual markers
words.root_gloss_range: making, appointing, causing, or rendering; local grammar selects completed divine appointment into a ritual category, not bare creation

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: accusative definite, fronted object (mafʿūl bih muqaddam) of jaʿalnāhā, or accusative of topicalization (ishtighāl)
preposition governing genitive shaʿāʾir; here partitive or classificatory (min al-bayāniyya or min al-tabʿīḍiyya)
genitive (governed by min), plural of shaʿīra; iḍāfa with Allāh
perfect 1st person plural with attached feminine pronoun -hā; Form II intensive/causative

words.prose: {{ar:جَعَلْنَٰهَا}} ({{tr:jaʿalnāhā}}) carries divine first-person plural agency inside the perfect verb and resumes {{ar:ٱلْبُدْنَ}} ({{tr:al-budna}}) with its attached pronoun. Its object-plus-{{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) complement selects appointment into the class of {{ar:شَعَائِرِ}} ({{tr:shaʿāʾiri}}), not creation of animals from nothing. The same verb also opens a frame that will be answered by {{ar:سَخَّرْنَٰهَا}} ({{tr:sakhkharnāhā}}): divine designation begins the rite and divine subjugation closes it, so human acts unfold inside a completed divine frame.

topics.headline: divine appointment, not bare creation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the animals already exist but are made to count as divine ritual markers.
topics.reason: QAC marks a doubly transitive verb with the hā object and min-complement, supporting appointment into a category.

topics.headline: appointment answered by subjugation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the whole rite framed by two matching divine perfect verbs, from appointment to serviceability and then gratitude.
topics.reason: The rows identify the opening/closing verbal frame and the same feminine pronoun object.

words.gloss_range: benefactive prepositional pronoun attaching the appointment to the addressed community
words.prose: {{ar:لَكُمْ}} ({{tr:lakum}}) makes the first beneficiary relation explicit: the animals are appointed for the addressees’ ritual benefit, not first presented as their property. As the first of three {{ar:لَكُمْ}} ({{tr:lakum}})-type refrains, it begins the chain of made-for-you, good-for-you, and subjected-for-you.

topics.headline: first beneficiary frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine appointment is oriented toward the addressees from the start of the ayah.
topics.reason: The lām phrase is a beneficiary phrase governed by the appointment clause and repeated later in the ayah.

words.gloss_range: partitive/classificatory preposition placing the offerings among God’s markers without exhausting that category

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: genitive (governed by min), plural of shaʿīra; iḍāfa with Allāh

words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) inserts the animals into {{ar:شَعَائِرِ}} ({{tr:shaʿāʾiri}}) without equating them with the whole class. The preposition lets the phrase mean both “among” and “as belonging to,” so the budn are identified as divine markers while other markers remain conceptually open.

topics.headline: class-entry among divine markers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the animals are one classified member of a broader divine-marker system, not the whole system.
topics.reason: QAC marks min governing the genitive plural with partitive or classificatory force.

words.gloss_range: plural construct for God’s sacred markers, tying perception/signhood to a divine genitive
words.root_gloss_range: perception, felt marking, hair/near-body signs, and ritual markers; local plural construct selects divine sacred markers

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: genitive (muḍāf ilayhi in iḍāfa with shaʿāʾir)

words.prose: {{ar:شَعَائِرِ}} ({{tr:shaʿāʾiri}}) names the animals as part of a plural system of sensed sacred markers. Its construct state waits for {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) to make the signs definite as God’s signs, not merely cultural symbols. The sh-ʿ-r field keeps perception close to the surface of the rite: these bodies are meant to be noticed, named, seen, and distributed. The phrase also resonates with the sacred-marker formula in 2:158, 5:2, and 22:32 while here specializing it to sacrificial animal bodies.

topics.headline: God’s sacred-marker construct
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the animals’ sign-status comes through a divine genitive construction, not through social convention alone.
topics.reason: The word is a genitive plural construct head completed by the following divine name.

topics.headline: perception made ritual
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels that the rite works as a perceivable marker, not as mute livestock management.
topics.reason: The root evidence links perceiving/marking and ritual symbols, and the local plural keeps that sign-system active.

topics.headline: known formula specialized to animals
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the wider sacred-marker formula while keeping this ayah’s referent to sacrificial bodies.
topics.reason: The cited formula recurs at 2:158, 5:2, and 22:32, but local syntax classifies the budn specifically.

words.gloss_range: proper-name genitive completing “God’s markers” and preparing the later “God’s name” construction
words.root_gloss_range: divinity, worship, and awe-turning; local proper-name genitive fixes God as source of the symbols or name

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: accusative definite (direct object of udhkurū), in iḍāfa with Allāh

words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) completes the first divine genitive: the markers belong to God’s sign-system. That completion prepares the later {{ar:ٱسْمَ}} ({{tr:isma}}) {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) construction, so the rite moves from God’s symbols to God’s name without changing its divine reference. The worship/awe pressure of the divine name supports that orientation, but the local job of the word is genitive attribution.

topics.headline: source of symbol-status
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the animals’ ritual status is attributed to God before any human act is commanded.
topics.reason: The proper name is genitive as the muḍāf ilayhi of the marker phrase.

topics.headline: worship and awe pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps worshipful awe in the background of the divine genitive without turning it into a separate local predicate.
topics.reason: The root discussion is meaningful but subordinate to the proper-name genitive function here.

topics.headline: from God’s symbols to God’s name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the local movement from divine classification to commanded divine naming, with 22:34 as a same-surah formula parallel.
topics.reason: Rows explicitly connect the two Allāh genitives and the 22:34 jaʿalnā to dhikr formula.

words.gloss_range: fronted beneficiary phrase in the nominal clause “for you, in them, is good”

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: fī + 3rd feminine singular pronoun referring to al-budna; locative preposition
nominative indefinite, subject of the nominal clause (lakum fīhā khayrun); delayed subject (mubtadaʾ muʾakhkhar)

words.prose: {{ar:لَكُمْ}} ({{tr:lakum}}) reopens the beneficiary line as a nominal benefit clause. By coming before {{ar:فِيهَا}} ({{tr:fīhā}}) {{ar:خَيْرٌ}} ({{tr:khayrun}}), it places the addressees in view before the delayed good is named, and the second repetition keeps sacred status from becoming abstract: the rite contains good directed to them.

topics.headline: benefit clause for the addressees
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah moves from divine classification to benefit located for the addressed community.
topics.reason: QAC marks the phrase as the second lām-pronoun and as the opening of a nominal benefit clause.

words.gloss_range: locative pronoun phrase anchoring the good in the animals and their rite
words.prose: {{ar:فِيهَا}} ({{tr:fīhā}}) sends the benefit back into the budn through the feminine pronoun. The preposition makes the good contained in the animals and their ritual use, not merely associated with them from outside.

topics.headline: good contained in the rite
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the good is located inside the sacrificial bodies and practice, not just attached as an external claim.
topics.reason: QAC marks fī plus a feminine singular pronoun referring back to the budn.

words.gloss_range: indefinite delayed subject naming open-ended benefit rather than a comparison
words.root_gloss_range: goodness, benefit, preference, and chosen value; local indefinite noun names open-ended benefit inside the rite
words.prose: {{ar:خَيْرٌ}} ({{tr:khayrun}}) is delayed and indefinite, so the clause asserts real good without itemizing it. In this setting it is not “better than” something else; it is open-ended benefit embedded in a divinely appointed rite. The kh-y-r field adds chosen value: the good is not vague positivity but benefit selected within the sacrificial practice.

topics.headline: unbounded embedded good
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the benefit is real but deliberately left unenumerated, covering ritual, material, and communal good.
topics.reason: QAC marks an indefinite nominative delayed subject in the nominal clause.

topics.headline: chosen value, not comparative better
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the goodness/choice field while local syntax blocks a comparative reading.
topics.reason: No compared item appears; the locative-benefactive clause selects absolute embedded benefit.

words.gloss_range: result/sequential fa moving from declaration of benefit into the first imperative
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is the hinge from declaration to procedure. Because the animals are God’s markers and contain good, the text immediately branches into the command to mention God’s name; the imperative is not a loose topic shift.

topics.headline: declaration becomes command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that naming follows as the consequence of classification and benefit, not as an unrelated instruction.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the particle as an explicative/branching fa before the imperative.

words.gloss_range: plural imperative commanding spoken remembrance of God’s name over the offerings
words.root_gloss_range: remembering, mentioning, and making present in speech; local imperative selects pronounced naming with remembrance pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: accusative definite (direct object of udhkurū), in iḍāfa with Allāh
genitive (muḍāf ilayhi in iḍāfa with shaʿāʾir)
ʿalā + 3rd feminine singular pronoun referring to al-budna; spatial/superimpositive preposition

words.prose: {{ar:ٱذْكُرُوا}} ({{tr:udhkurū}}) turns the beneficiaries into actors. The imperative governs {{ar:ٱسْمَ}} ({{tr:isma}}) {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) as the spoken content and {{ar:عَلَيْهَا}} ({{tr:ʿalayhā}}) as the target, so remembrance and verbal mention converge in a consecrating speech-act. The Form I command asks the addressees themselves to pronounce the name, not to make someone else remember, while the variant recollection reading remains useful as an inward contrast. The formula also returns from 22:28 and 22:34, and across the boundary from 22:35 the root shifts from hearts responding to mention into people actively mentioning over the animals.

topics.headline: addressees commanded to name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rite requires the addressed community to perform a verbal naming act over the animals.
topics.reason: QAC marks a 2mp imperative, with the following name phrase as object and over-phrase as target.

topics.headline: remembrance becomes speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees dhikr as both remembered devotion and spoken ritual performance, not one or the other.
topics.reason: The object name phrase and ritual target select verbal invocation while the root keeps remembrance active.

topics.headline: Form I against causative or reflexive alternatives
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the local command is direct mention, while the variant shows how the force could shift toward internal recollection.
topics.reason: The standard form is CV:I; the variant and Form II evidence qualify but do not replace the local form.

topics.headline: liturgical formula and boundary shift
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the 22:28 and 22:34 naming formula and the shift from inward trembling in 22:35 to outward commanded speech in 22:36.
topics.reason: Rows supply concrete same-surah references and the boundary movement from passive mention to active command.

words.gloss_range: accusative construct object specifying the divine name as the object of mention
words.root_gloss_range: name, elevation, and naming/marking disputes; local construct object selects the already-known divine name

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: genitive (muḍāf ilayhi in iḍāfa with shaʿāʾir)

words.prose: {{ar:ٱسْمَ}} ({{tr:isma}}) makes the command precise: the object is the name, not a vague Godward thought. As a construct head, it becomes definite through {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}). The s-m-w/elevation and w-s-m/marking dispute remains productive here, because pronouncing the name both raises and marks the sacrificial act, but local syntax keeps the focus on the already-known divine name, not assigning a new name.

topics.headline: the name as direct object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ritual requires a specific verbal object: God’s name.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as accusative object of the imperative and construct with the following divine name.

topics.headline: elevating and marking pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels naming as an elevating and marking act while avoiding the overclaim that a new name is assigned.
topics.reason: The derivational dispute supports imagery, but the local noun is the object “name” rather than a causative naming verb.

topics.headline: recurring name formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the phrase as part of the surah’s sacrificial naming protocol, including 22:28 and 22:34.
topics.reason: The row gives explicit same-surah formula recurrences.

words.gloss_range: proper-name genitive specifying whose name is invoked
words.root_gloss_range: divinity, worship, and awe-turning; local proper-name genitive fixes God as source of the symbols or name
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) completes the name construct and locks the speech-act to God’s own name. Together with the earlier divine-name genitive at word 7, it maps the rite from God’s signs to God’s name: what the animals are and what must be said over them share the same divine reference.

topics.headline: God as owner of the invoked name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the consecrating speech is not generic sacred language but God’s name specifically.
topics.reason: QAC marks the proper name as genitive after the construct head ism.

topics.headline: symbols-to-name echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the local echo from God’s markers to God’s name as the rite moves from classification to performance.
topics.reason: Rows explicitly connect the two genitive constructions at words 7 and 14.

words.gloss_range: superimpositive target phrase placing the spoken name over the sacrificial animals
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْهَا}} ({{tr:ʿalayhā}}) fuses the preposition with the pronoun that points back to the budn, making the animals the surface target of the naming. The superimpositive force lets the spoken name be imagined as placed over them, so speech functions as a covering consecration rather than a comment merely about them.

topics.headline: speech placed over the animals
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the name is directed over the animal bodies, giving the speech-act spatial ritual force.
topics.reason: QAC marks ʿalā plus feminine pronoun referring to the budn, attached to the naming command.

words.gloss_range: accusative participial circumstantial state: the animals standing/aligned during naming
words.root_gloss_range: lining, ranks, and ordered formation; local participial ḥāl selects standing/aligned posture during naming
words.prose: {{ar:صَوَآفَّ}} ({{tr:ṣawāffa}}) fixes the animals’ visible state during the naming. As a ḥāl, it describes posture rather than issuing a separate command: the bodies stand aligned while the name is mentioned over them. Variant readings sharpen the apparatus: {{ar:صَوَآفَّ}} ({{tr:ṣawāffa}}) selects ṣ-f-f rows, while purity or one-leg-bound readings would shift the visual emphasis. The ranked-scene echoes at 37:1 and 61:4 make the alignment feel like ordered formation, and even the doubled final sound reinforces the stacked visual texture.

topics.headline: circumstantial aligned posture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that naming is tied to the animals’ arranged state, not only to the later slaughter.
topics.reason: QAC marks an accusative plural active participle functioning as ḥāl during the naming.

topics.headline: alignment selected over purity variants
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that standard alignment governs the local reading while accepted variants show possible purity or bound-posture emphases.
topics.reason: Standard QAC root is ṣ-f-f; variants are apparatus that qualify the visual field without replacing it.

topics.headline: ordered ranks and stacked sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears and sees the shift from interior piety to an exterior ordered formation, with 37:1 and 61:4 as rank echoes.
topics.reason: Rows supply concrete rank parallels and a boundary shift into visible ritual posture.

words.gloss_range: sequential fa advancing from naming/posture into the falling-condition phase
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) moves the rite into its next phase. The particle keeps naming, posture, and eventual collapse in an ordered sequence rather than letting the fall appear as an unrelated later event.

topics.headline: next procedural phase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah manages the rite stage by stage, from naming into the condition of fall.
topics.reason: QAC marks this fa before the temporal clause as introducing a new sequential phase.

words.gloss_range: certain temporal condition governing the fall and setting the threshold for eating
words.prose: {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}) turns the fall of the sides into the expected threshold for the next commands. With a perfect verb after it, the particle points forward to a certain procedural event: speech first, visible completion second, eating and feeding third.

topics.headline: certain temporal threshold
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the fall is expected protocol, not a hypothetical contingency.
topics.reason: QAC marks idhā as a temporal adverb governing the perfect verb and pointing to the response clause.

topics.headline: speech to fall to distribution
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ritual chain pivot from naming to physical completion to consumption and feeding.
topics.reason: Rows explicitly identify the fa-idhā construction as the pivot between ritual phases.

words.gloss_range: feminine perfect verb for the sides falling, with obligation/due-ness resonating from the root
words.root_gloss_range: falling, settling, becoming due, and obligation; local verb selects flank-collapse as the threshold that makes eating and feeding due

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nominative plural (fāʿil of wajabat) + possessive pronoun -hā referring to al-budna

words.prose: {{ar:وَجَبَتْ}} ({{tr:wajabat}}) agrees with {{ar:جُنُوبُهَا}} ({{tr:junūbuhā}}), so the visible sides are the grammatical subject of the fall. The root makes the physical collapse do legal-procedural work: when the flanks settle, eating and feeding become due. The hapax status gives unusual weight to this single visible threshold, and the boundary from 22:35 is pointed: hearts tremble inwardly when God is mentioned, then flanks fall outwardly after God’s name is pronounced.

topics.headline: sides as falling subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the text watches the flanks fall, not an abstract death event.
topics.reason: QAC marks feminine singular agreement with the plural body-part subject.

topics.headline: falling becomes due-ness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees physical collapse as the moment that establishes the next obligation/permission.
topics.reason: Root evidence supports falling and due-ness, while the local clause makes fall the threshold for the commands.

topics.headline: unique clipped threshold and body-part bridge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the fall as a marked, singular threshold linking 22:35’s trembling hearts to 22:36’s falling flanks.
topics.reason: Rows supply hapax status, sound texture, and the concrete 22:35 boundary relation.

words.gloss_range: plural possessive body-part subject: their sides/flanks as visible evidence of completion
words.root_gloss_range: side, flank, avoidance, and ritual distance; local plural possessive names the animals’ sides as visible subject of falling

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: perfect 3rd feminine singular (agreeing with junūbuhā); hapax legomenon in the Quran

words.prose: {{ar:جُنُوبُهَا}} ({{tr:junūbuhā}}) is the subject of {{ar:وَجَبَتْ}} ({{tr:wajabat}}), so the ayah makes body-parts carry the procedural evidence. The plural spreads the collapse across the sacrificial bodies, while the hā pronoun keeps the budn in view. The j-n-b field of side, avoidance, and ritual distance colors the moment: the flank that had to be kept apart becomes the visible point after which eating is allowed. The 39:56 echo remains a contrast about not neglecting the divine side/right, not a replacement for the local animal flanks.

topics.headline: flanks as procedural evidence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that visible flanks, not a generic death statement, authorize the next stage.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as nominative fāʿil with a possessive pronoun.

topics.headline: side and ritual distance pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the transition from ritual distance to permitted contact through the side-root field.
topics.reason: The root field is meaningful, but local denotation remains the animals’ physical sides.

topics.headline: 39:56 side echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear a side/due-right resonance with 39:56 while keeping this clause about fallen sacrificial flanks.
topics.reason: The row gives a concrete recurrence at 39:56, but local syntax is a body-part subject.

words.gloss_range: answer fa linking the completed fall to the eating command

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: temporal adverb introducing a conditional-temporal clause; ẓarf zamān governing the perfect verb wajabat

words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is the response marker to the {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}) clause. It keeps eating dependent on the completed fall: when the sides have fallen, then the addressees may move into consumption.

topics.headline: fall answered by eating
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that consumption is controlled by the visible completion signal.
topics.reason: QAC marks the particle as fa al-jazāʾ introducing the apodosis of the idhā clause.

words.gloss_range: plural imperative of sanctioned eating from the offering, structurally paired with feeding others
words.root_gloss_range: eating and consumption, including metaphorical appropriation; local imperative with partitive source selects sanctioned eating from the offering

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: min + 3rd feminine singular pronoun referring to al-budna; partitive
imperative 2nd person masculine plural of Form IV ʾaṭʿama; command to feed others

words.prose: {{ar:كُلُوا}} ({{tr:kulū}}) authorizes the addressees’ own intake after the fall, but it does so with {{ar:مِنْهَا}} ({{tr:minhā}}), not a direct object. That partitive source keeps eating limited and makes room for distribution. The simple eating imperative then pairs with {{ar:أَطْعِمُوا}} ({{tr:aṭʿimū}}), separating personal consumption from the stronger duty to make others eat. The 22:28 echo confirms this as part of a same-surah slaughter-etiquette formula.

topics.headline: sanctioned eating from, not all of
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that eating is permitted/instructed as part of the rite but limited to a portion from the animals.
topics.reason: QAC marks a 2mp imperative followed by a partitive source phrase.

topics.headline: consumption not exploitative taking
topics.reader_payoff: The reader distinguishes legitimate sacrificial eating from the broader root’s negative appropriation uses.
topics.reason: The following partitive and feeding command narrow the root’s consumption range to sanctioned food intake.

topics.headline: self-consumption bound to feeding others
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that private benefit cannot close the rite because eating is immediately coordinated with feeding.
topics.reason: Rows identify the paired imperatives and the distribution ethics generated by min plus Form IV feeding.

topics.headline: 22:28 eating-and-feeding echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the same-surah formula in 22:28, now tied to the budn’s fallen sides.
topics.reason: The row gives the concrete 22:28 echo.

words.gloss_range: partitive/source phrase limiting personal eating and opening distribution
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْهَا}} ({{tr:minhā}}) says eat from them, not simply eat them. The preposition makes the animals the source of food while reserving the whole from being privately consumed; grammatically, the phrase opens space for the feeding command that follows.

topics.headline: partitive source for sharing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grammar itself reserves distribution by limiting personal consumption to a portion.
topics.reason: QAC marks min plus hā referring to the budn, with partitive force.

words.gloss_range: coordinating waw joining feeding to eating as a co-present duty

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) reopens the sequence toward others. By coordinating {{ar:أَطْعِمُوا}} ({{tr:aṭʿimū}}) with {{ar:كُلُوا}} ({{tr:kulū}}), it gives self-directed eating and other-directed feeding the same syntactic frame, so distribution is not an optional afterthought.

words.prose: {{ar:أَطْعِمُوا}} ({{tr:aṭʿimū}}) turns the same addressees into agents of other people’s nourishment. Its Form IV causative does more than say “share a meal”; it makes them cause the recipients to eat, with {{ar:ٱلْقَانِعَ}} ({{tr:al-qāniʿa}}) and {{ar:ٱلْمُعْتَرَّ}} ({{tr:al-muʿtarra}}) as coordinated object classes. The taste/food root links their own permitted eating to the obligation to provide edible nourishment, and 22:28 plus 76:8-9 broaden the ethical resonance without displacing the local sacrifice scene.

topics.headline: active duty to feed recipients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sacrificers are responsible for making others eat, not merely leaving food available.
topics.reason: QAC marks a 2mp Form IV imperative governing two coordinated object classes.

topics.headline: taste experience becomes provision

topics.reason: Root evidence and boundary rows connect eating/taste to causative feeding and received provision distributed.

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْقَانِعَ}} ({{tr:al-qāniʿa}}) is accusative under {{ar:أَطْعِمُوا}} ({{tr:aṭʿimū}}) and definite, so it names a recognized recipient class. The q-n-ʿ field keeps contentment, humble asking, and veiled need together: this is the needy person whose need may be restrained rather than displayed. Its active participle form contrasts with {{ar:ٱلْمُعْتَرَّ}} ({{tr:al-muʿtarra}}), so the feeding command covers both concealed/restraint-coded need and exposed need.

topics.headline: recognized restrained-needy class

Its ʿ-r-r field makes need visible as affliction or self-presentation, while the ʿ-r-y variant adds the image of naked exposure. The oblique variant shows how syntax could weaken the object role, but the standard accusative locks this exposed-needy category into the feeding command. Together with {{ar:ٱلْقَانِعَ}} ({{tr:al-qāniʿa}}), it completes a two-pole map of restrained and exposed need.

words.prose: {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhālika}}) gathers the entire preceding ritual sequence, not one isolated noun. The distal pointer compresses naming, falling, eating, and feeding into one recoverable referent before {{ar:سَخَّرْنَٰهَا}} ({{tr:sakhkharnāhā}}) and {{ar:لَعَلَّكُمْ}} ({{tr:laʿallakum}}) {{ar:تَشْكُرُونَ}} ({{tr:tashkurūna}}) state source and purpose.

words.prose: {{ar:سَخَّرْنَٰهَا}} ({{tr:sakhkharnāhā}}) closes the divine-action frame opened by {{ar:جَعَلْنَٰهَا}} ({{tr:jaʿalnāhā}}). Its Form II makes serviceability causative and intensive: the animals are made usable for the addressees, not merely found useful. The s-kh-r root can include mockery, but this form selects harnessing/subjugation while keeping the power relation audible. Same-surah echoes in 22:37 and 22:65, and wider cosmic subjugation scenes such as 14:32-33 and 16:12, broaden the scope, but here the subjugation is localized in sacrificial animals.

topics.headline: animals made serviceable for you
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the animals’ usefulness is a divine making-serviceable relation directed toward the addressees.
topics.reason: QAC marks a Form II perfect with hā object and following beneficiary phrase.

topics.headline: power relation without ridicule
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the root’s power relation while the local Form II blocks the mockery sense.
topics.reason: Root branches include mockery, but QAC form and local valency select subjugation/harnessing.

topics.headline: cosmic subjugation localized to animals
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the budn included in a larger serviceability refrain, with 22:37 and 22:65 as same-surah echoes, while the local object remains the sacrificial animals.
topics.reason: Rows give concrete parallels at 22:37, 22:65, 14:32-33, and 16:12; local pronoun still refers to the budn.

topics.headline: designation-to-subjugation inclusio
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees divine agency frame the entire procedure, from “We appointed them” to “We subjected them.”
topics.reason: Rows identify the matching first-person plural perfect verbs and the register shift into direct commissioning.

words.prose: {{ar:لَكُمْ}} ({{tr:lakum}}) attaches the closing subjugation to the addressees. As the third beneficiary phrase, it completes the chain: appointed for you, good for you, subjected for you. The same community described in 22:35 is now directly addressed as beneficiary and actor.

topics.headline: third for-you completion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah’s backbone of repeated benefit: designation, embedded good, and subjugation are all oriented toward the addressees.
topics.reason: QAC marks the third lām-pronoun phrase and the rows map it to the repeated beneficiary chain.

topics.headline: described group becomes addressed beneficiary

topics.reason: The row explicitly identifies the boundary pronoun shift.

words.gloss_range: expectative/purpose particle with addressee pronoun opening the gratitude outcome clause
words.prose: {{ar:لَعَلَّكُمْ}} ({{tr:laʿallakum}}) prevents the ayah from ending at human use. The particle carries hope-language and purpose together in divine speech, assigning the intended outcome directly to the addressees: the whole sequence is aimed toward their gratitude.

topics.headline: gratitude as intended outcome
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that naming, falling, eating, feeding, and subjugation are teleologically aimed at gratitude.
topics.reason: QAC marks laʿalla plus pronoun governing the predicate tashkurūna, and the rows treat divine laʿalla as purpose/hoped result.

topics.headline: modality bound to you
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the hoped-for outcome is assigned to the same addressed community carried through the ayah.
topics.reason: The particle and the kum pronoun are fused in the surface form.

words.gloss_range: imperfect second-person plural gratitude as the ongoing endpoint of the ritual arc
words.root_gloss_range: gratitude, acknowledgement, opposite of denial, and abundant response to benefit; local imperfect marks ongoing gratitude as outcome

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: expectative particle laʿalla + 2nd person masculine plural pronoun; introduces the hoped-for outcome

words.prose: {{ar:تَشْكُرُونَ}} ({{tr:tashkurūna}}) lands the ayah on ongoing gratitude, not a single utterance after eating. The imperfect under {{ar:لَعَلَّكُمْ}} ({{tr:laʿallakum}}) frames gratitude as the intended outcome rather than a direct imperative. The sh-k-r field opposes denial and turns received benefit into acknowledged return; even the image of an animal thriving on little fits the sacrificial-animal setting, where humans should turn bestowed serviceability into abundant thanks. As the final word, it makes gratitude the interpretive landing of signs, benefit, naming, falling, eating, feeding, and subjugation.

topics.headline: ongoing gratitude, not one act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that gratitude is the continuing result the rite is meant to produce, not a one-time command.
topics.reason: QAC marks an imperfect 2mp verb under laʿallakum rather than an imperative form.

topics.headline: gratitude as acknowledged benefit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees gratitude as moral acknowledgement of received serviceability, the opposite of denial.
topics.reason: Root evidence links shukr with opposed denial, and the taskhir-shukr pair makes gratitude the expected feedback.

topics.headline: animal-root image of abundant response
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the sacrificial-animal irony: humans should respond abundantly to benefit as the root image describes thriving on little.
topics.reason: The branch image is locally apt because the ayah is about sacrificial animals and benefit.

topics.headline: final word of the ritual arc
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the whole ayah converge on gratitude as its final interpretive landing, with 22:77 as a broader exhortatory closing parallel.
topics.reason: Rows identify the final-word position and formulaic pairing of making/subjugation with gratitude.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The made-for-you, ritual-sign, eat, feed, subjected-for-you, and thank sequence.
baseline_models.mechanism: A dedicated animal is assigned the status of public ritual sign; its ordered availability moves material benefit through self-consumption and feeding others, while gratitude returns recognition to the giver. The repeated for-you language therefore establishes entrusted use, not bare possession.

activation_trace.role: The dedicated sacrificial animal supplies the material body that enters the benefit circuit.
Assignment to a status makes the animal's ritual usefulness a conferred role rather than an ownership fact.
A legible ritual marker converts livestock into a sign whose handling bears public meaning.
Actual eating directs part of the animal into the offerers' nourishment.
Feeding another extends the benefit beyond the offerers and makes distribution integral to the rite.
Directed tractability enables the ordered use while locating its source outside human power.
Acknowledgment of benefaction is the intended human return produced by the completed circuit.

changed_reading.before: The verse grants an animal for sacrifice and permits charity afterward.
changed_reading.after: The verse constitutes an entrusted circuit in which a marked body becomes shared nourishment and the resulting recognition, rather than ownership, is the human response.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The consecutive aligned, sides-fall, then-eat constructions.
baseline_models.mechanism: Linear bodily alignment is maintained until a definite fall onto the sides marks completion; only then does eating begin. Posture and aspect therefore create a visible threshold between living sign and distributable food.

activation_trace.role: Alignment on an even line supplies the stable pre-threshold posture.
Falling supplies the completed event that releases the next stage.
The bodily side gives the fall a concrete final orientation rather than an abstract death notice.
Eating is the action gated by the completed bodily fall.

changed_reading.before: The verse lists slaughter and eating instructions.
changed_reading.after: The verse scripts a controlled state transition: aligned living bodies become fallen bodies, and only across that observable boundary do they become food.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired recipient nouns immediately after the command to feed.
baseline_models.mechanism: One recipient root carries both contentment and asking, while the other carries exposure to benefaction and arrival at another's precinct seeking a need. The pair resists making one style of self-presentation the price of food.

activation_trace.role: Contentment supplies the recipient whose need may remain restrained or non-insistent.
Asking for benefaction keeps the same recipient term open to explicit request rather than fixing it as silent need.
Exposure to another's good supplies a recipient who presents need without requiring a formal verbal demand.
Coming to another's precinct as seeker supplies mobility and arrival as a second way need becomes visible.

changed_reading.before: The verse names two fixed welfare categories, usually separated by whether they ask.
changed_reading.after: The paired terms preserve a spectrum from contained need through exposed or arriving need, so distribution cannot depend on one approved performance of poverty.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The movement from good and feeding to the final purpose of gratitude.
baseline_models.mechanism: The gratitude inventory includes a little input producing a visible effect, fullness, and fresh growth. Coupled with feeding, this makes gratitude materially diagnostic: received good should become perceptible sufficiency or new benefit beyond the first recipient.

activation_trace.role: Generosity and gift supply the good received rather than merely an advantageous property.
Feeding another gives the received good an outward, observable effect.
A small provision yielding visible condition supplies the productivity test for gratitude.
Fullness and abundance supply the bodily endpoint that shared food can produce.
Fresh shoots supply an image of benefit continuing beyond its initial material input.

changed_reading.before: Gratitude is a verbal or inward response appended to the sacrifice.
changed_reading.after: Gratitude is also the visible yield of the gift: food becomes another person's sufficiency, so acknowledgment is embodied as propagated benefit.

context_deltas.mechanism: Elsewhere, experienced good can become the unstable condition of edge-worship, whereas animal provision is explicitly paired with feeding need and the surah closes by joining enacted good to flourishing. These cues revise the focus's good-for-you from private advantage into benefit completed by circulation.

activation_trace.role: Beneficial good anchors the focus claim that the animal contains advantage for the addressees.
Feeding others provides the focus's own route by which advantage leaves private possession.
Experienced benefit supplies the unstable private-good model on which conditional worship can rest.
Allocated gift reframes the animal as provision received before it can be redistributed.
Material need supplies the destination that tests whether received benefit has become shared good.
Good as an action, not merely an experience, turns the focus benefit into a commandable practice.
Flourishing and lasting success supply the result of doing, rather than hoarding, the good.

structural_cues: 22:11 makes received good a test of whether worship is merely conditional.
22:28 repeats the eat-and-feed sequence while explicitly naming provision and poverty.
22:77 places doing good immediately before the prospect of flourishing.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a contrast between experienced benefit, allocated provision, need, and enacted good. I infer that circulation is the directional test converting benefit into good. A live alternative is that these are parallel ethical themes rather than a definition of the focus's good.

changed_reading.before: The good in the animal is the benefit its owners may take from it.
changed_reading.after: The animal's benefit becomes good-for-you precisely through a circuit that reaches need; private advantage alone remains spiritually unstable.

context_deltas.mechanism: The sanctuary is made equally accessible to the one who stays and the one from outside, and the preceding feeding instruction names material need. This social geometry sharpens the focus recipient pair: the sacrificial meal performs equal access across settled, restrained, exposed, and arriving positions.

activation_trace.role: Contented restraint supplies the recipient whose need can remain socially quiet.
Arrival at another's precinct seeking a need supplies the mobile or outside recipient.
Equality between two positions supplies the sanctuary's access rule and the meal's social measure.
Staying in devoted attendance supplies the settled side of the access contrast.
The outside or non-urban position supplies the arriving side that must receive equal access.
Concrete lack prevents the equality model from remaining only spatial or ceremonial.

structural_cues: 22:25 describes the sanctuary as made for people on equal terms across resident and outsider positions.
22:27 has pilgrims arrive from every deep route.
22:28 turns the gathered provision toward a person in material need.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies equal sanctuary access, incoming pilgrims, and recipient terms with restrained and arriving branches. I infer that the shared meat materializes the sanctuary's equality. A live alternative is that the resident-outsider and recipient pairs are adjacent but not socially coextensive.

changed_reading.before: Feeding the two recipients is an isolated charitable addition to sacrifice.
changed_reading.after: The meal enacts the sanctuary's equal-access order by carrying its provision across differences in residence, mobility, and how need appears.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah places universal lowering before a sanctuary sequence of standing, bowing, and prostration, then contrasts it with the uncontrolled fall of association. Against that field, the animal's aligned stance and completed side-fall can function as an embodied, ordered descent under the divine name rather than a merely mechanical collapse.

activation_trace.role: Even alignment supplies the animal's ordered upright phase.
Completed falling supplies the animal's controlled descent.
Lowering in submission supplies the surah-wide bodily field in which nonhuman beings also participate.
Bodily standing supplies the first posture in the sanctuary's ordered devotional descent.
Bending and lowering the head supplies the transitional posture between standing and full lowering.
Head-lowering and bodily inclination complete the sanctuary's ordered posture sequence.
A noisy, disordered fall supplies the negative counterpart to the focus's bounded descent.
Plunging into an abyss supplies the uncontained trajectory from which the named ritual fall differs.

structural_cues: 22:18 includes earthbound creatures within universal prostration.
22:26 orders sanctuary bodies as standing, bowing, and prostrating.
22:31 figures association as uncontrolled falling and plunging.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two posture sequences and a contrast between ordered lowering and uncontrolled fall. I infer an embodied analogy between worshippers' descent and the animal's aligned fall. A live alternative is that the focus posture remains entirely procedural and the resemblance is only visual.

changed_reading.before: Alignment steadies the animals and their fallen sides merely indicate death.
changed_reading.after: The stance-to-side sequence can make the animal itself a bodily sign of ordered surrender, sharply distinguished from the disintegrating fall used to image association.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah explicitly denies that flesh or blood reaches God and affirms protected, reverent orientation as what reaches. This separates two outputs already latent in the focus: material goes horizontally through eating and feeding, while Godward response is nonmaterial recognition and guarded conduct.

activation_trace.role: Feeding another anchors the humanward destination of the material body.
Acknowledgment anchors the nonmaterial response directed back toward the giver.
Reaching supplies the explicit destination test, negated for materials and affirmed for piety.
Literal flesh supplies one material explicitly excluded from a Godward transfer.
Literal blood supplies the second material explicitly excluded from a Godward transfer.
Placing oneself under protection supplies the guarded orientation that can reach where flesh and blood cannot.

structural_cues: 22:37 uses the same destination verb for the negated material pair and the affirmed piety.
The focus sends flesh toward eaters before the next ayah denies its Godward arrival.
22:37 continues from subjection to magnification, guidance, and good-doing.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an explicit material-versus-piety destination contrast. I infer a two-vector economy: flesh moves toward people and reverent recognition toward God. A live alternative is that the next ayah only corrects sacrificial theology, though the adjacent feeding command still supports the destination split.

changed_reading.before: The sacrifice and its distributed meat jointly constitute an offering transferred toward God.
changed_reading.after: No material is transferred to God: the body is routed to human nourishment, while piety and grateful magnification are the Godward outcome.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same subjection formula later encompasses earth and ship, while the sky is held from falling except by permission and the frame closes with tenderness, mercy, and human ingratitude. The focus's permitted side-fall is thus one bounded release inside a larger regime of holding and care, not a license for unqualified mastery.

activation_trace.role: Directed tractability anchors the human availability whose limits the later cosmic use exposes.
The animal's actual fall supplies the local release placed against the later held fall.
Cosmic directed availability broadens subjection beyond livestock and locates all human use within one giver's ordering.
Holding back supplies restraint as the complement to making something available.
Falling and coming to rest supply the cosmic counterpart whose release remains permission-bound.
Tender compassion supplies the governing quality around cosmic holding and availability.
Merciful softness makes care, not domination, the containing frame for subjection.
Covering over a blessing supplies the direct negative of the focus's intended gratitude.

structural_cues: 22:65 repeats the focus's subjected-for-you formula on a cosmic scale.
The same ayah couples availability with holding the sky from a permissionless fall.
22:66 follows life, death, and renewed life with the charge that the human is deeply ungrateful.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies shared subjection language, a held-versus-permitted fall, compassion, and the gratitude contrast. I infer that granted use is structurally bounded by the giver's restraint and care. A live alternative is that cosmic preservation illustrates power without directly limiting sacrificial agency.

changed_reading.before: Subjection means the animal has been placed under unilateral human control.
changed_reading.after: Subjection means permissioned availability within a compassionate holding-and-release order; gratitude requires using that delegated capacity without converting it into absolute mastery.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah's early earth sequence moves from lifeless dryness through activation, growth, and new emergence, while its later life-death-life sequence prevents death from being the final horizon. Joined to the focus gratitude branches of visible yield and fresh growth, the animal's fall becomes an obligation against waste: ended animal life must be converted into nourishment and renewed social sufficiency.

activation_trace.role: The completed fall supplies the apparent endpoint whose material aftermath the model follows.
A small input producing visible condition supplies the focus's own yield logic.
Fresh growth supplies the focus branch that lets gratitude resonate with regeneration.
Dried lifelessness supplies the apparently exhausted material state from which change begins.
Earth and vegetation stirring with life supply activation after apparent stillness.
Nourishment and growth supply the intermediate conversion from received input to increased life.
Plant emergence supplies the visible new yield produced by the regenerative sequence.
Living creaturehood at both ends supplies the wider life horizon around the intervening death.
Loss of life supplies the real interruption that the surrounding sequence refuses to make ultimate.

structural_cues: 22:5 renders apparently dead earth as a staged material transformation into growth.
22:66 places death between two divine givings of life.
The focus sends the fallen body immediately into eating and feeding, not disposal.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies regenerative earth, life-death-life, and a focus branch where gratitude appears as growth. I infer a material ethic of conversion from fallen body to sustaining food. A live alternative is that resurrection and vegetation only establish divine power and should not be mapped onto sacrificial redistribution.

changed_reading.before: Once the animal falls, distribution is a useful aftermath of completed death.
changed_reading.after: The fall creates a duty of regenerative use: the ended life must not terminate in waste but become food, sufficiency, and a visible yield of gratitude.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah twice says that a rite is assigned to every community, links sacrificial practice to voiced naming and surrender, and then blocks ritual contest. The focus's detailed choreography is therefore a concrete assigned form within plural communal rites, while its unifying axis is acknowledgment of the one giver and ethical surrender.

activation_trace.role: Assignment to a status anchors the focus choreography as something instituted rather than naturally universal.
Assigning each community a form supplies institutional plurality across communities.
Sacrificial devotion supplies the specific ritual domain in which the plurality operates.
Voiced mention supplies a shared orientation that can persist across different assigned forms.
Naming as designation supplies the common referent around which the rites are ordered.
Handing over and surrender supply the common human posture beneath formal plurality.
Practiced devotion supplies the repeated claim that every community inhabits an assigned rite.
Mutual pulling between sides supplies the contest that ritual plurality is not meant to generate.

structural_cues: 22:34 assigns a rite to every community and immediately directs all toward one deity and surrender.
22:67 repeats the every-community assignment and tells opponents not to contest the matter.
The focus supplies one unusually concrete posture, timing, and distribution choreography.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated communal assignment, one divine orientation, and a prohibition on ritual contest. I infer that formal specificity is local embodiment rather than a claim that every community must share identical mechanics. A live alternative is that the plural assignments are historical stages and the focus remains the final uniform form.

changed_reading.before: The focus gives the universal sacrificial template against which all rites should be measured.
changed_reading.after: The focus gives one concretely assigned communal form whose universal core is naming the giver, surrendering, and turning provision into ethical benefit rather than enforcing identical choreography.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates a non-dominant mapping from name toward visible marking and a marked public season. It remains anchored to the focus's name word and its explicit ritual-sign construction. Downstream prose should present it as branch resonance, not replace the ordinary lexical sense of uttering the divine name.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The ritual-sign noun and the command to voice the name over the aligned animals.

activation_trace.role: A ritual marker supplies the already public, legible status of the animal.
Voicing on the tongue supplies the audible act by which the status is declared.
Name as designation supplies the ordinary identifying force of the utterance.
A visible identifying mark supplies the exploratory sense that naming publicly reclassifies the body.
A marked season of assembly supplies the exploratory public-event scale of the naming act.

changed_reading.before: Naming is an uttered label placed over an otherwise unchanged act of slaughter.
changed_reading.after: The uttered name can also be heard as publicly marking body and gathering as belonging to a sacred season, making the act socially legible before the body falls.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it links the surah's smallest creature and its anti-idolatry parable to the handling of a very large sacrificial body. It remains anchored to the focus's claim of subjection and the parable's creation, rescue, weakness, and seeking branches. Downstream prose should qualify it as a scale-reversal critique of autonomous mastery, not as an additional slaughter rule.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The claim that the large sacrificial animals were made tractable for the addressees.

activation_trace.role: Great bodily size supplies the large-scale creature that humans appear able to control.
Directed tractability anchors that control as granted availability rather than self-originating human force.
Creative origination supplies the capacity denied to the invoked powers even at tiny scale.
The fly supplies the tiny creature whose agency reverses the apparent hierarchy of control.
Inability to extract something from another's hold supplies the failure of autonomous rescue and control.
Lack of strength supplies the explicit diagnosis beneath pretended mastery.
Seeking supplies both sides of the failed transaction and exposes dependence rather than command.

changed_reading.before: Humans control the large animals because human strength makes them masters of lesser creatures.
changed_reading.after: Control of the large body is itself a received gift: the fly reversal exposes every claim of autonomous mastery, so subjection should produce gratitude and restraint rather than self-deification.

strongest_changes: The post-focus destination contrast makes the material body humanward nourishment while piety and grateful magnification are the Godward outcome.
Repeated subjection plus the held-versus-permitted cosmic fall turns human control into bounded, compassionate availability rather than absolute mastery.
Sanctuary equality and the recipient-root ambiguity make feeding an enactment of access across settled, arriving, restrained, and exposed need.
The standing-to-fall sequence can operate as an embodied sign of ordered surrender, contrasted with the surah's uncontrolled fall of association.
Repeated assignment of rites to every community relocates universality from identical mechanics to naming, surrender, and ethical use of provision.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah field did more than explain sacrificial procedure: controlled fall, equal access, plural rites, material non-arrival, cosmic holding, regeneration, and the fly's scale reversal transformed the focus into a compact model of delegated power, public redistribution, and embodied surrender.
remaining_uncertainties: The analogy between animal posture and worshipper posture is visually and sequentially strong but remains reader-supplied.
The resident-outsider pair and the two food recipients need not denote identical social groups.
The regenerative model is a material and ethical analogy, not a claim that killing itself causes spiritual renewal.
The name-to-mark-and-season activation depends on a non-dominant mapped root and must remain explicitly exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Vertical order becomes horizontal distribution.** `ب د ن B003/B001` supplies sacrificial animal and bodily frame; `ص ف ف B001` straight rows; `و ج ب B001/B002` falling and due fixity; `ج ن ب B001` bodily flanks. The standing bodies fall, then become food. I infer that the visible transition from aligned life to grounded flesh converts ritual orientation into shared provision. Sacrifice reads as ordered redistribution rather than destruction alone.
2. **Two postures of need are included.** `ق ن ع B001/B002` preserves both contented acceptance and humbled asking; `ع ر ر B004` is approaching for need. The paired recipients follow the general command to feed. I infer that need may remain quiet or become visible approach, and provision must reach both. The verse keeps these readings distinct while making gratitude (`ش ك ر B001`) recognition expressed through distribution.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 22:73's fly parable sharpened the animal hierarchy: creatures placed under human use still expose human and idol incapacity, preventing *taskhīr* from becoming absolute ownership.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A living body is converted from emblem to shared provision.** Fixed `ٱلْبُدْن` activates `ب د ن:B003` (sacrificial animal), `شَعَائِر` uses `ش ع ر:B006`, and `صَوَافّ` uses `ص ف ف:B001` (straight-row arrangement). After named mention, `وَجَبَت` activates `و ج ب:B001` (falling), and the body moves into eating and feeding. Recipients preserve two modes: `ق ن ع:B001` (contented acceptance) or `B002` (humbled asking), and `ع ر ر:B004` (approaching for need). `22:35` supplies outward expenditure and `22:37` denies that flesh itself reaches God. The packet supplies posture, fall, and distribution; I infer a controlled transformation of bodily mass into social nourishment. The rite's mechanism culminates in access for differently situated needy people.
2. **Subjection has an explicit beneficiary and purpose.** Fixed `سَخَّرْنَاهَا` activates `س خ ر:B001` (bringing under command for a purpose), and `تَشْكُرُون` activates `ش ك ر:B001` (recognizing a favor) with `B002` (little sustenance showing effect). I infer that human control is legitimate here because its stated output is recognition and sharing. The ayah does not leave domination as an end in itself.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later `22:37` explicitly blocks a material-transfer reading. That correction makes the fixed naming, falling, eating, and feeding the carrier of guarded orientation rather than a gift of flesh or blood to God.

inter_ayah_rows.note: Explicitly forbids eating that over which Allah's name has not been mentioned, the direct negative counterpart to the focus formula.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Pairs eating from divine produce with giving its due at harvest, illuminating provision as carrying an obligation of distribution.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Identifies livestock as both carrying animals and food and commands eating from Allah's provision without following Satan.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Its enumeration of livestock pairs supplies background for the animal categories used in sacrificial provision.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Places sacrifice together with prayer, life, and death as wholly for Allah, directly grounding the focus's exclusive naming of Him.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The promise that gratitude increases divine favor supports the focus's concluding call to give thanks.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Describes livestock as created for warmth, benefits, and food, closely matching the focus's divinely provided animal benefits.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The cattle are a source of drink and nourishment, a secondary animal-provision parallel.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Its ban on what has been dedicated to other than Allah reinforces the exclusive divine orientation of the sacrifice.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The purification of the House for circumambulation, standing, bowing, and prostration establishes the sacred setting of the ensuing rites.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The command to proclaim the Hajj directly introduces the pilgrimage movement in which the focus's sacrificial rite occurs.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It closes the surah with the chosen community's religion and command to strive for Allah, providing the larger covenantal frame for its rites.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Livestock provide drink, many benefits, and food, closely paralleling the focus's animal provision before its ritual specification.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The messenger-command to eat good things and act righteously gives a broad ethical frame for consuming provision.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Allah's creation of livestock for human possession directly precedes their taming for riding and eating.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Ibrahim's commanded sacrifice of his son supplies a major Quranic sacrifice scene, marked by submission to Allah's command.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The son is ransomed with a great sacrifice, directly presenting divinely supplied sacrificial substitution.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Allah makes livestock for people to ride and eat, closely paralleling the focus's divinely subjected animal provision.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The rider's remembrance that Allah subjected the mounts and the ensuing gratitude gives a related subjection-and-thanks formula.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Feeding food to the poor, orphan, and captive provides a direct ethical parallel to the focus's command to feed others.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Its rebuke for not encouraging the feeding of the poor supplies a negative counterpart to the focus's distribution command.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Feeding during famine gives a concentrated instance of the social duty that the focus attaches to sacrificial food.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The condemnation of withholding encouragement to feed the poor contrasts directly with the focus's required feeding.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The command to pray to the Lord and sacrifice is a compact, direct parallel for worship-directed sacrifice.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Its required giving to relatives, orphans, and the needy provides a broad distributional counterpart to feeding from the sacrifice.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Feeding a needy person as compensatory practice supplies a legal parallel for provision directed to those in need.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Its identification of recipients for spending gives a general social frame for the focus's command to feed others.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The instruction to spend from good earnings and what Allah brings forth supplies a broad ethic of sharing provision.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Its command to do good to relatives, neighbors, and needy people gives a general ethical horizon for sacrificial distribution.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Lawful food from the sea is a distinct food-law parallel, without the focus's naming or sacrificial setting.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It rejects arbitrary claims that the contents of certain livestock are restricted by sex, clarifying divine rather than invented food rules.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Its specified food prohibitions and ban on dedication to other than Allah provide a close legal boundary for animal consumption.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The historical livestock restrictions on the Jews are a secondary food-law contrast to the focus's permitted animal provision.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The messenger's making good things lawful and impure things forbidden offers a broad food-law frame.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Benefits from livestock skins, wool, and hair extend the Quranic presentation of animals as divine provision.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The cattle are said to provide further benefits and drink, continuing the provision sequence immediately after riding and eating.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The creation of eight livestock pairs gives background to the animal kinds available as divine provision.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Failure to urge feeding the poor is condemned, forming a clear negative counterpart to the focus's command to feed.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: A recognized claim in wealth establishes a broad economic basis for provision owed to others.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: It identifies the needy and deprived as holders of that claim, generally paralleling the focus's food distribution.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The admission of not feeding the poor supplies another explicit negative counterpart to the focus's feeding command.

identity_judgment.rationale: Dal ifadesi, insanin govdesini veya beden kismini anlatan ortak cekirdegi destekler. Kayitlar bunu bir butun beden olarak da, bas ve uclar disinda kalan govde olarak da kullanir; cansiz govde anlami ancak acik baglamda girer.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Cekirdek, zihin veya kisilik degil fiziksel govdedir; zirh, adaklik hayvan, sisme ve yaslilik bu dala ait degildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Bare dal oldugu icin tanim temel ada baglidir; zirh veya adaklik hayvan gibi baska adlasmis kullanimlar buraya tasinmaz.

concept_map.definition: Insanin fiziksel govdesi, kimi kayitta butun vucut gibi, kimi kayitta bas ve el-ayak uclari disinda kalan ana govde gibi sinirlanan bedensel varliktir.

facets.statement: Anlamin merkezi, insanin elle tutulur fiziksel govdesidir.
Bazi aktarimlar kapsami butun beden, bazilari bas ve uclar disindaki ana govde olarak daraltir.
Ruhsuz govde anlami genel cekirdekten degil, acik soylem baglamindan dogar.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak malzeme fiziksel insan govdesini verir. Kayitlar kapsami bazen tum beden, bazen bas ve uclar disindaki ana govde olarak sunar; cansizlik ancak baglamla belirginlesir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Fiziksel govdeyi anlatan genel karsiliktir; bas ve uclar disindaki sinirlama gerektiginde tanimla birlikte okunmalidir.

error_profile.preserves: Fiziksel insan govdesi cekirdegini korur.
error_profile.loses: Butun beden ile ana govde arasindaki kaynak farkini tek basina gostermez.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Ana beden kismina vurgu yapan baglamlarda dogal karsiliktir.

error_profile.preserves: Ana fiziksel govde fikrini korur.
error_profile.loses: Butun insan bedeni olarak genis kullanimi disarida birakir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Yalniz baglam ruhsuz fiziksel varligi acikca gerektiriyorsa kullanilir.

error_profile.preserves: Ruhsuz fiziksel govde uzantisini korur.
error_profile.loses: Genel canli insan govdesi kapsamini disarida birakir.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: insanin govdesi veya bas ve uclar disindaki ana bedensel kisim

error_profile.preserves: Fiziksel varlikla ilgili genel sezgiyi korur.
error_profile.loses: Bas ve uclar disindaki ana govde sinirini aciklamaz.
error_profile.adds: Gundelik Turkcede soyut, egitsel veya sporla ilgili yan alanlar cagrabilir.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: B001 varligin bedensel kismini verir; B004 o kismin hacim, etlilik veya sismanlik niteligini anlatir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal korunacak veya ortulecek fiziksel govdedir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Dal ifadesi, govdeyi saran veya govde uzerinde bulunan kisa zirh adini dogru yansitir. Kayitlar bunu govdenin kendisiyle karistirmaz; adlandirma iliskisi zirhin govdeyi kapsamasindan veya onun uzerinde bulunmasindan gelir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal koruyucu giysidir; fiziksel govde, adaklik hayvan, sismanlik ve yaslilik anlamlari buraya girmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Bare dal olarak adlasmis zirh anlamini tanimlar; govde kelimesinin temel anlamindan genel bir giysi anlamina genisletilmez.

concept_map.definition: Govde uzerinde tasinan veya govdeyi saran kisa zirh turudur; adlandirma, koruyucu parcanin govdeyle temas ve kapsama iliskisine baglidir.

facets.statement: Cekirdek, savasta giyilen kisa bir zirh veya zirh benzeri koruyucu parcadir.
Adlandirma, zirhin govdeyi sarmasi veya govde uzerinde bulunmasi ile aciklanir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak anlatim, kisa bir zirh adini verir. Malzeme, bu adin govdeyi saran veya govde uzerinde duran koruyucu parcadan kaynaklandigini aciklar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Govde uzerinde tasinan veya govdeyi saran koruyucu zirh anlaminda uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Kisa koruyucu zirh cekirdegini korur.

error_profile.preserves: Govde uzerindeki zirh iliskisini korur.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal belirli, kisa ve govdeyle iliskilendirilen zirhi anlatir; komsu dal ise genel koruyucu zirh veya savas giysisi alanidir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal kisa zirh olma ozelligini vurgular.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal koruyucu zirhin varligini anlatir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komsu dal zirh, migfer veya koruyucu ortuden yoksun olma durumunu anlatir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Ikisi de savasta govdenin koruyucu donanimla iliskisini degerlendirir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: B002 govde uzerindeki koruyucu parcayi adlandirir; komsu dal bu tur korumanin bulunmamasini anlatan karsi kutuptur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal govde uzerine giyilen koruyucu nesnedir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komsu dal korunan fiziksel govdenin kendisidir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Iliski, zirhin govdeyi sarmasi veya onun uzerinde bulunmasindan dogar.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: B002 giysiyi veya koruyucu nesneyi verir; B001 bu nesnenin uzerine geldigi fiziksel govdeyi verir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Dal ifadesi, belirli ibadet veya adama baglaminda ayrilan deve, sigir veya erkek deve gibi buyuk hayvani anlatir. Kayitlar bunun koyuna uygulanmadigini ve cogul bicimin de bu adaklik hayvanlari gosterdigini belirtir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal adak ve kesim icin ayrilan buyuk hayvani anlatir; govde, zirh ve yalnizca sismanlik anlamlariyla karistirilmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Bare dal olarak adlasmis hayvan adini tanimlar; temel govde anlami veya yalniz sismanlik buraya aktarilmaz.

concept_map.definition: Adak veya dinsel kesim icin ayrilan deve, sigir ya da erkek deve gibi buyuk hayvandir; kapsama koyun girmez ve cogul bicim bu tur hayvanlari topluca anlatir.

facets.statement: Cekirdek, adak veya dinsel kesim icin ayrilmis buyuk hayvandir.
Kapsam deve, sigir ve erkek deve gibi buyuk hayvanlarla sinirlidir; koyun dahil edilmez.
Aktarimlar bazen ayrilma yerini veya kesim yerini vurgular, fakat cekirdek adaklik buyuk hayvanda kalir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak malzeme, adak veya rituel kesim icin ayrilan buyuk hayvan adini verir. Kapsama deve ve sigir turleri girer; koyun disarida kalir, cogul bicim de bu siniftaki hayvanlari anlatir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Deve veya sigir gibi dinsel kesime ayrilan buyuk hayvani anlatmak icin uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Adak icin ayrilmis buyuk hayvan cekirdegini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Hayvan turlerinin aciklanmasi gereken baglamlarda daha uzun ama daha belirgin karsiliktir.

error_profile.preserves: Kesime ayrilma ve buyuk hayvan kapsamlarini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Cogul bicimde topluca anilan hayvanlar icin uygundur, fakat buyuk hayvan siniri metinde korunmalidir.

error_profile.preserves: Adak icin ayrilmis hayvan fikrini korur.
error_profile.adds: Koyun gibi daha kucuk hayvanlari da cagrabilir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal adaklik buyuk hayvanin belirli adini ve tur sinirini verir.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: B003 hayvanin adaklik buyuk hayvan olarak sinifini verir; komsu dal kesim zamani veya olayinin adiyla ayrilir.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komsu dal devenin bogaz bolgesinden kesilmesi eylemini anlatir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Ikisi de deve veya buyuk hayvan kesimi senaryosunda birlikte bulunabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: B003 nesne olan adaklik hayvani adlandirir; komsu dal o hayvana uygulanabilecek kesme eylemini adlandirir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Adak, rituel kesim ve kesme eylemi alanindaki en yakin komsular secildi; mezar hayvani veya kesim araci gibi adaylar cekirdegi daha dogrudan aydinlatmadigi icin yayinlanmadi.
branches.what_is_ar: البدنة من الإبل أو البقر أو البعير في الهدي والأضاحي وجمعها بدن
branches.what_is_not_ar: الشاة؛ الجسد والدرع؛ السمن مجردا من الهدي أو الأضحية
branches.source_phrase_ar: البدنة التي تهدى للبيت (maqayis)؛ البدنة ناقة أو بقرة تنحر بمكة (sihah)؛ البدنة تقع على الناقة والبقرة والبعير الذكر مما يجوز في الهدي والأضاحي ولا تقع على الشاة (tahdhib)؛ البدن جمع البدنة التي تهدى (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Dal, govdenin iriligi, et tutmasi ve sismanlik anlamini dogru yakalar; ancak ortak kayit icinde ayni soylem parcasinin yaslilikla aciklandigi bir gelenek de vardir. Bu nedenle tanim, yalniz hacim ve etlilik alaninda kalmali, yaslilik okumasini B005 ile sinirda tutmalidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal iri veya sisman govde durumudur; yaslilik ancak ayrica desteklenirse baska dala aittir.
